subject.title: config: use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should OpenClaw accept timestamped config backup filenames, and if so must existing `.bak.N` recovery files be preserved or converted instead of pruned on first write?
rationale: Changing shipped config recovery files affects existing users' rollback points, and the repository policy treats config migration and fallback behavior as compatibility-sensitive product direction.

options.title: Require migration-safe timestamp backups
options.body: Proceed only with a branch that preserves or converts existing numbered backups into the bounded timestamped retention set and proves the upgrade path.

options.title: Accept timestamp-only cleanup
options.body: Allow the new cleanup to prune legacy numbered backups on first write, explicitly owning the recovery-retention loss as a product choice.

options.title: Keep the numeric ring
options.body: Decline the naming change for now and keep the shipped numbered backup contract documented in doctor guidance.

recommendation.title: Require migration-safe timestamp backups
recommendation.body: Proceed only with a branch that preserves or converts existing numbered backups into the bounded timestamped retention set and proves the upgrade path.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest sampled history for config compatibility policy and nearby backup-rotation tests.
